drc-writer-first-pass.SANCTIONS: The Council renewed measures from resolution 2293 (2016) until 1 July 2024. It confirmed that paragraph 1 of resolution 1807 (2008) continues to apply to nongovernmental entities and individuals in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
drc-writer-first-pass.EXPERTS: Council extended Group of Experts mandate to 1 Aug 2024, reviewing by 1 July 2024. Midterm report due 30 Dec 2023; final report 15 June 2024. Monthly Committee updates except report months.
drc-writer-first-pass.RUSSIA: Russia voted for renewal, arguing sanctions must be adjusted or lifted when outdated or impeding state-building. It welcomed the Council's December 2022 removal of the DRC notification requirement and reiterated opposition to illegitimate unilateral measures.
drc-writer-first-pass.DRC: The DRC welcomed renewed measures targeting non-state actors, assured government cooperation with the Group of Experts, requested an objective approach, and confirmed timely submission of its confidential stock-management report.
drc-writer-first-pass.overlap: Russia and the DRC shared support for renewed sanctions. Russia voted in favour as a Council member, while the DRC gave a statement as the affected state following the vote.
drc-writer-first-pass.with_russia: The Council renewed sanctions under resolution 2293 (2016) until 1 July 2024 [SANCTIONS]. Measures in resolution 1807 (2008) continue for nongovernmental entities in the DRC [SANCTIONS]. Russia voted for renewal [RUSSIA], arguing sanctions should adjust when outdated or impeding state-building [RUSSIA]. The Council extended the Group of Experts mandate to 1 August 2024 [EXPERTS]. It requested a midterm report by 30 December 2023 and a final report by 15 June 2024 [EXPERTS]. The Group must send monthly updates to the Committee, excluding report-due months [EXPERTS]. Russia welcomed the December 2022 removal of the DRC notification requirement [RUSSIA] and reiterated opposition to illegitimate unilateral sanctions [RUSSIA].
drc-writer-first-pass.with_drc: The Council renewed sanctions under resolution 2293 (2016) until 1 July 2024 [SANCTIONS:1–3], maintaining paragraph 1 of resolution 1807 (2008) for nongovernmental entities in the DRC [SANCTIONS:1–3]. The Group of Experts mandate extended to 1 August 2024 [EXPERTS:5–6], with a midterm report due 30 December 2023 and final report by 15 June 2024 [EXPERTS:5–6]. The DRC, as the affected state, welcomed the renewed targeting of nongovernmental actors [DRC:2–3], assured government cooperation with the Experts [DRC:2–3], requested an objective approach [DRC:2–3], and confirmed timely submission of its confidential stock-management report [DRC:2–3].
drc-writer-first-pass.both_positions: The Council renewed sanctions under paragraphs 1–6 of resolution 2293 (2016) until 1 July 2024 [SANCTIONS]. Measures targeting nongovernmental entities and individuals in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, per paragraph 1 of resolution 1807 (2008), remain applicable [SANCTIONS]. Russia voted in favour [RUSSIA], arguing sanctions should adjust or lift when outdated or hindering state-building [RUSSIA]. It welcomed the December 2022 removal of the DRC notification requirement [RUSSIA] but opposed illegitimate unilateral sanctions [RUSSIA]. The DRC, as the affected state, welcomed the renewed targeting of nongovernmental entities and individuals [DRC]. It assured government cooperation with the Group of Experts [DRC], requested an objective approach [DRC], and confirmed timely submission of its confidential stock-management report [DRC].
